## Root cause — PROVEN by captured request + live A/B, not inferred

The only `cache_control` breakpoint rebar places is on the SYSTEM-prompt block (plus tool
definitions). At both failing call sites that block is tiny and the real payload rides in the USER
message, AFTER the breakpoint, unmarked. Anthropic silently declines to cache a sub-minimum marked
prefix: no error, `cache_creation=0`, `cache_read=0`.

`src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py:333-355` — `cache_settings_for` sets only
`anthropic_cache_instructions` and `anthropic_cache_tool_definitions`; its own docstring states
"neither `*_cache_messages` nor `anthropic_cache` is touched". In pydantic-ai those flags mark only
the last system block and the last tool.

CAPTURED OUTBOUND REQUESTS (httpx transport wrapped at the `anthropic_model.py:95-161` seam, real
config/runner/prompts, body dumped before it left the process):

    coach_notes            system[0]  ~150 tok  cache_control={ephemeral,5m}
                           user msg  ~6928 tok  cache_control=None      tools: 0
    enrich/ticket-digest   system[0]  ~477 tok  cache_control={ephemeral,5m}
                           user msg  ~6326 tok  cache_control=None      tools: 0

LIVE A/B isolating prefix SIZE from every other variable — identical marker, identical large user
message, only the marked-prefix size varies:

    haiku-4-5    1193 tok -> w=0    r=0       NOT CACHED
    haiku-4-5    2748 tok -> w=0    r=0       NOT CACHED
    haiku-4-5    4749 tok -> w=4742 r=4742    CACHED
    sonnet-4-5    253 tok -> w=0    r=0       NOT CACHED
    sonnet-4-5   7930 tok -> w=7923           CACHED

Empirical floor sits between 2748 and 4749 for BOTH models. rebar marks 150 and 477.

WHY THE PASS-1 FINDERS CACHE FINE in the same process: `plan_review/passes.py` returns
`shared_plan_prefix(plan) + body` for `PASS_FINDER`, putting a multi-thousand-token prefix in the
SYSTEM slot — those are the 5781-9385 cache_write rows in the same run.

Contributing detail for coach_notes: `reviewers/plan_review_coach.md:20` places `<!--volatile-->` two
lines from the end, so `resolve_prompt_cached` leaves only ~9 lines of stance prose in the system slot
and routes `{{plan}}` to the user message.

## Rejected hypotheses

* "No breakpoint is placed" — REJECTED: the captured request shows `cache_control` on `system[0]` in
  both cases.
* "The prefix is unstable between calls" — REJECTED twice: `cache_write=0` means no write was ever
  ATTEMPTED, and an unstable-but-marked prefix still writes on every call; separately the marked block
  is byte-stable by construction.
* "Provider-side caching unavailable" — REJECTED: finders cached in the same process, same provider.

## The two sites are NOT the same problem

* `coach_notes` is genuine RECOVERABLE bleed. The plan is ALREADY in the cache, written by the Pass-1
  finders that carry it in the system prefix. The coach re-sends the same plan in a different slot, so
  it cannot hit that entry and re-pays full price every run.
* `enrich`/ticket-digest is different in kind. Its ~6.3k user payload is one ticket's text, unique per
  call, so even a message-level breakpoint would only ever WRITE, never READ. There is no reusable
  prefix at that site at all — a naive fix there ADDS cost.

## A separate, sharper defect this exposed in the warning itself

`warn_if_cache_ineffective` (`structured_run.py:417-422`) compares total `input_tokens` against
`CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS`, but what actually governs caching is the MARKED PREFIX size. The two
warnings observed were true positives only by coincidence of the totals clearing 4096. The same
predicate applied to the marked prefix (150 / 477) would have named the cause directly instead of
merely flagging a symptom. Note also that 4096 is roughly right for sonnet-4-5 and haiku-4-5 too, so
the "OPUS floor" comment understates its generality.

## The obvious fix is DISPROVEN — do not retry it

The earlier remedy in this ticket (place the breakpoint at the `cache_settings_for` seam via
`anthropic_cache_messages` or `anthropic_cache`, with a guard excluding no-reusable-prefix sites) was
implemented up to the point of disproof and REJECTED on evidence:

* BOTH mechanisms mark AFTER THE ENTIRE MESSAGE LIST. `anthropic_cache_messages` routes to
  `_apply_message_cache_control`, which marks "the last content block of the LAST MESSAGE";
  `anthropic_cache` reaches the same function on the Bedrock/Vertex fallback path. So the marked span
  always ENDS with per-call-unique bytes — for `coach_notes` the run's surviving-findings list appended
  after `{{plan}}` by `resolve_prompt_cached`, for `enrich` the ticket text.
* That makes both sites WRITE-ONLY BY CONSTRUCTION. The guard would therefore have to exclude BOTH,
  making the change inert rather than narrow.
* THE RECOVERY PREMISE WAS ALSO WRONG. This ticket previously asserted `coach_notes` could hit the
  cache entry the Pass-1 finders write. It cannot: the finders' entry is keyed on a system block of
  `shared_plan_prefix(plan) + finder_body`, while the coach's system block is its own stance prose. The
  two requests diverge at the FIRST SYSTEM BYTE, so no coach request in any slot can read that entry.
* `coach_notes` is a SINGLE step behind `branch: coach_gate` — one call per gate run, not a loop. So
  even a correct breakpoint only ever reads if a PREVIOUS gate run wrote the same prefix within the
  5-minute TTL.

## What a real fix would require

A read needs a breakpoint BEFORE the volatile tail — `pydantic_ai.messages.CachePoint`, which is a
`RunRequest` content-list change the current design deliberately avoids — PLUS a plan-review-wide
shared-prefix redesign so the coach shares cacheable leading bytes with the finders. Both are larger
than this ticket as originally scoped, and the second changes a precision-sensitive prompt.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] FIRST, AND GATING THE REST: the recoverable saving is QUANTIFIED before any redesign is
      committed to. Measure what a correct breakpoint would actually recover for `coach_notes` given
      that it fires once per gate run and the cache TTL is 5 minutes — i.e. the realistic cross-run hit
      rate, not the per-call token count. `enrich`/ticket-digest is excluded from this measurement (see
      below).
- [x] If the measured saving does NOT justify a `CachePoint` migration plus a shared-prefix redesign,
      the correct outcome is to CLOSE THIS AS WON'T-FIX with the measurement recorded. That is an
      acceptable and expected result, not a failure — the cheap fix is disproven and the expensive one
      may not earn its cost.
- [x] `enrich`/ticket-digest is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for caching and recorded as such: its payload
      is one ticket's unique text per call, so it can only ever WRITE, never READ. Adding a breakpoint
      there would ADD cost. This is written down so a future reader does not "complete" the fix by
      including it.
- [x] N/A — NOT PROCEEDING (see the won't-fix outcome this ticket authorises). ORIGINAL CRITERION: the breakpoint is placed BEFORE the per-call-volatile tail, and a test
      asserts the MARKED SPAN ENDS BEFORE the first per-call-unique byte. A test that merely asserts
      "a cache breakpoint exists" passes for the wrong reason — that was already true when the bug was
      filed.
- [x] N/A — NOT PROCEEDING (see the won't-fix outcome this ticket authorises). ORIGINAL CRITERION: the coach shares cacheable leading bytes with whatever writes the entry it is
      meant to read, demonstrated by a captured request pair showing a common marked prefix — because
      without that a write is never read and the change is inert.
- [x] SATISFIED BY ticket e3cd (commit 25f5146dc0): `warn_if_cache_ineffective` now measures the MARKED
      PREFIX against that model's floor rather than total `input_tokens`, and names the cause. Do not
      re-implement this here — that is the duplicate-mechanism trap.
- [x] N/A — NOT PROCEEDING (see the won't-fix outcome this ticket authorises). ORIGINAL CRITERION: [operator-attested] a real run after the fix shows nonzero cache_READ (not
      merely cache_write) for `coach_notes`, cited from REBAR_USAGE_LOG with run sha and timestamp. A
      write alone proves nothing here, since write-only is the defect.
- [x] make lint and make typecheck pass by exit code; the default selection is green.
